newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong gold ends up on overseas buying.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong gold ends up on overseas buying.

text.p: Hong Kong gold ended a shade up from New York's Monday close after continued fund shortcovering and in spite of healthy European sales, bullion dealers and traders said on Tuesday.
"We saw some American buying earlier in the day," said one gold dealer, noting it had likely spilled over from overnight fund shortcovering in New York.
Bullion ended at US$381.60/382.10 an ounce on Tuesday against New York's US$381.50/381.90 close on Monday.
Some gold dealers reported limited Japanese selling of gold and platinum.
The Hong Kong bullion market also saw producer selling from South Africa and Australia, gold traders said, noting there was selling interest near $382 per ounce.
The spot gold price dipped even further when European markets opened, gold sources said.
"The Europeans haven't seen gold reach these resistance levels in a long time and there was fresh selling interest," said a bullion dealer at an international bank.
Gold traders said sentiment was turning somewhat bullish as gold broke resistance at $381 per ounce.
"Before it was all doom and gloom and now everyone is saying it'll go to $385 per ounce," said another dealer at an international bank's Hong Kong office.
Local gold ended HK$15 higher at HK$3,514 a tael.
The carryover charge at the Chinese Gold and Silver Exchange Society dropped to -8.00 from its previous fix at -6.00 BULLION -
